caveats: Requires dynamic_upstreams plus passive health_checks configured: without dynamic upstreams the write runs only in Provision before serving starts, so concurrent requests only read the field.
Requires concurrent requests served on separate goroutines (net/http per-request goroutines, outside this tree).
The race is on the PassiveHealthChecks.logger pointer field itself, not inside zap.Logger, which is safe for concurrent use.
subclaims.reason: The only write to Passive.logger is R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:1081 in provisionUpstream, and with dynamic upstreams it runs per request via proxyLoopIteration at R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:464-466 on request-serving goroutines (ServeHTTP at R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:403, value receiver but shared pointer field). Concurrent requests therefore race write-write on the shared field, each storing a distinct *zap.Logger from Named, and write-read against countFailure's loads at R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/healthchecks.go:462,487 and the forgetter goroutine's loads at R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/healthchecks.go:472,487, reached per request via R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:544,815,822. Neither side holds a lock: Handler.connectionsMu at R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:210 guards only connections. No happens-before rules the interleaving out: independent request goroutines have no ordering between them, and the go statement at R5/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/healthchecks.go:469 orders only spawner to spawned, not one request's write against another request's forgetter.
